facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.
facts.text: In the Rigveda, solar hymns celebrate the Sun and the dawn goddess Ushas as self-evident cosmic forces sustained in nature without the use of anthropomorphic idols.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: There is no murti and no priest mediating the worship. The offering goes directly to Surya and Chhathi Maiya, made by the family itself.
facts.text: Folk tradition in Bihar asserts that Chhathi Maiya has no idol because she embodies formless nature and cosmic solar rays that cannot be confined within a stone statue.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Many in Bihar trace the practice of standing in the river directly to him — and to Anga, his kingdom, present-day Bhagalpur.
facts.text: Local lore traces the custom of standing waist-deep in river water to offer arghya directly to the Mahabharata warrior Karna in the ancient region of Anga.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The figurative manifestations of the Sun were found for the first time in 200BC Bodh Gaya railings.
facts.source_name: Patna University Department of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology
facts.text: Archaeological analysis of the Bodh Gaya sandstone railing dating to 200 BCE revealed the earliest known visual relief of the Sun god in Bihar riding a horse-drawn chariot, confirming ancient regional solar iconography.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Archaeological and art-historical scholarship has documented representations of the goddess in the Mathura sculptural tradition during the Kushan period.
facts.source_name: Journal of the Indian Society of Oriental Art
facts.text: An art-historical survey published in 1969 established that while Shashthi acquired anthropomorphic sculpted images in Mathura during the 1st to 3rd centuries CE, eastern riverine solar rituals intentionally maintained aniconic worship using natural produce.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Built during the 8th century by Chandravanshi King Bhairavendra Singh, with an inscription from 1437 documenting the dedication of the temple.
facts.text: Surveys by the Archaeological Survey of India document that the historic Deo Sun Temple in Bihar features solar iconography dating between the 8th and 15th centuries CE but contains no sanctum idol of Chhathi Maiya, serving instead as an open gathering site for river and pond offerings.

instagram.caption:
Chhathi Maiya ki murti kyun nahi hoti?
Na pandit, na mandir, seedha Surya ko arghya.
Rigveda, Mathura ki murtiyan aur Deo Surya Mandir, sab saath rakhkar dekhiye.
Aap kya maante hain, Maiya Usha hain ya gaon ki maa-devi?
Maa ko bhejo jo har saal ghat par arghya deti hain.
